full_judgment: 9. Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division committed error as it has failed to consider that the plaintiffs proved their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land by oral and documentary evidence and the appellate Court below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice as it did not consider the evidence on right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is not tenable in law. He further submits that the High Court Division committed error in not considering that lower appellate court shifted the burden of proof upon the plaintiffs wrongly about alluvion and dilluvion of suit land. There was no such case or evidence on record rather, defendant No. 28 claimed in the written statement that suit land was alluviated and dilluviated, so burden of proof lies upon defendant No. 28 who asserts the fact. The lower appellate court wrongly mere surmise and conjecture found that plaintiffs failed to prove the alluvion and dilluvion and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He next submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the appellate Court below misdirected itself in law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court without reversing its findings. He also submits that the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not well founded as the High Court Division did not consider that the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below is result of non-consideration, misreading and misinterpretation of the evidences on record. He finally submits that only the contesting defendant No.28 who was Tohshilder of local revenue office who created forged, fabricated and antedated documents of lease though he as Government servant was not entitled to get settlement but the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court below failed to consider it and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law.
